raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

cuDNN 9.11 removed support for GPUs older than Turing: Maxwell, Pascal and Volta, i.e. compute capability below 7.5 ([9.11.0 release notes](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/backend/v9.11.0/release-notes.html), "no longer supported"). The backend's heuristics still return plans on such a GPU, and those plans build and pass `check_support()`. The graph fails only at `execute()`.

On a V100 (cc 7.0), driver 580.178, develop 97b7bc31, a plain half `conv_fprop` graph gives:

| cuDNN | result |
|---|---|
| 9.10.2 | runs, max error 0.031 against `torch.nn.functional.conv2d` |
| 9.11.0, 9.11.1 | `execute` fails with `CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` |
| 9.27.0 | `execute` fails with `err 209 no kernel image is available for execution on the device` |

PyTorch rejects this pair up front (cuDNN ≥ 9.11 with SM < 7.5 in `torch.backends.cudnn`). That check also aborts this repo's test session on such a GPU, because `conftest.py` prints `torch.backends.cudnn.version()`.

## Change

- `graph_interface.h`: a new `check_backend_supports_sm_` declines with `GRAPH_NOT_SUPPORTED` when the backend is 9.11 or newer and the target SM is below 75. The message names the backend, the target SM and cuDNN 9.10 as the last pre-Turing release.
  - `check_support()` runs it after resolving the target SM.
  - `create_execution_plans()` runs it before the heuristics query, so a graph that goes straight to `build_plans()` fails before execute.
  - The target SM is the device's SM or the `sm_version` an AoT graph sets. A deviceless graph without a target keeps `sm_version` 0 and is not checked.
- `test/python/conftest.py`: prints PyTorch's cuDNN version only when PyTorch can initialize it.
- New `test/python/core/graph/test_pre_turing_target.py`:
  - targets SM 52/61/70/72 through `sm_version=` and expects the decline from both `create_execution_plans` and `check_support`;
  - checks that an SM75 target is not declined by this rule;
  - skips on cuDNN ≤ 9.10.

## Tests

- **V100 (cc 7.0), cuDNN 9.27:**
  - New test: 4 failed on develop (`DID NOT RAISE`), 5 passed with this change.
  - The conv graph above now declines at `check_support` with the new message instead of failing at `execute`.
- **V100, cuDNN 9.10.2:** the conv graph runs as before; the new tests skip.
- **B300 (cc 10.3), cuDNN 9.27:**
  - New test: 4 failed on develop, 5 passed.
  - `-m L0` over `test/python/core`, `conv`, `norm` and `fe_api`: 3174 passed, 13 failed with this change. The same 13 tests fail on develop, all in `test_native_backend_lowering` and `test_knob_vocabulary`; their failure list is identical with and without this change apart from the 4 new tests.
- `pre-commit` on the touched files passes (clang-format, black).

`Context` starts `target_sm_version` at −1, so `== 0` skipped device discovery for a graph without a target. The plan gate now resolves any non-positive target from the device first. A deviceless graph without a target still skips the check.

`test_cudnn_911_declines_the_current_pre_turing_device` covers the omitted-target case. It runs only on a GPU below compute capability 7.5: it builds the graph without `sm_version` and expects `create_execution_plans()` itself to decline.

| | `test_pre_turing_target.py` |
|---|---|
| develop 97b7bc31 | 5 failed (the four explicit targets and the omitted target), 1 passed |

Reviewed `2b4361682fdd` against base `97b7bc3128d6`.

Thank you for your contribution! The explicit-target guard works in independent C++ checks. I found one nonblocking P2 gap for an omitted target. Approval remains deferred while current-head CI and the Style/Security approval gates are pending.

**[P2] Resolve the default -1 target before the plan gate** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/2b4361682fddf47734a039449283731bdf556413/include/cudnn_frontend/graph_interface.h#L3368))

Context initializes target_sm_version to -1, and both Graph() and pygraph() without sm_version retain that value. This == 0 branch therefore skips device discovery for the normal omitted-target case; check_backend_supports_sm_(-1) then succeeds. On a pre-Turing device, callers that use create_execution_plans() followed directly by build_plans() still miss the promised early rejection. check_support() does resolve the target, so that path is protected. Handle all unset/nonpositive target values here, preserve the best-effort behavior when no device exists, and add an omitted-target regression case.

Evidence: Exact-head C++ host probe with backend 91100 and a simulated SM70: default target -1 made zero device queries and passed create_execution_plans({}); explicit target 0 made one query and returned the new error. Both default and zero targets were rejected by check_support(). Source confirms build_plans() does not call Graph::check_support(). The empty-mode probe isolates the guard and does not claim GPU execution on SM70. Attribution: Incomplete coverage in the new early-rejection path; the unsupported backend/device execution failure predates this PR.

Checked runtime version gating and L0 collection (checklist D22/E01). Compiled independent C++17 probes against the exact head and base headers. On native SM100 with cuDNN 9.26, all six head planning cases behaved as expected: explicit SM52/61/70/72 were rejected by both entrypoints, while SM75 and the omitted target passed. The same base probe accepted all four old targets, demonstrating the guard's effect. These were planning checks, not convolution execution tests. Thirteen host guard cases covered backend 9.10/9.11 boundaries, explicit targets, omitted/zero targets and unavailable-device behavior. Backend/device queries were stubbed for these cases; they confirm the omitted-target gap but do not establish native V100 coverage. The release boundary matches the official [cuDNN 9.11 release notes](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/cudnn/backend/v9.11.0/release-notes.html). No execution kernel, reduction order or deterministic route changes in this diff.

Limitations: No independent native pre-Turing run, older-backend run, Python extension rebuild or full regression suite. The author's V100 and SM103 results remain separate evidence. Current-head Style/Security workflows require maintainer action, and current-head GPU CI has not run. No workflow approval or CI access workaround was attempted.

files.patch:
@@ -604,7 +604,10 @@ def pytest_configure(config):
         print(f"PyTorch Version: {torch.__version__}")
         print(f"PyTorch Path: {torch.__file__}")
         print(f"PyTorch CUDA Version: {torch.version.cuda}")
-        print(f"PyTorch cuDNN Version: {torch.backends.cudnn.version()}")
+        try:
+            print(f"PyTorch cuDNN Version: {torch.backends.cudnn.version()}")
+        except RuntimeError as e:  # e.g. cuDNN 9.11+ on a GPU below SM75, which PyTorch refuses to initialize
+            print(f"PyTorch cuDNN Version: unavailable ({str(e)[:120]})")
     try:
         # The CuTe DSL wheel and the CUDA toolchain it bound (its cu12 / cu13 flavour, picked by the driver): the compiler floors of the
         # OSS kernels (python/cudnn/AGENTS.md Rule 7) read THIS, never torch.version.cuda, so a lane's log names the compiler it ran.

@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""cuDNN 9.11 removed Maxwell, Pascal and Volta (compute capability below 7.5). A graph that targets one must
+decline at plan creation and at check_support: the backend's heuristics still return plans for it that build and
+only fail at execute (CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED on a V100 with cuDNN 9.11.0, 9.11.1 and 9.27.0)."""
+
+import cudnn
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.L0,
+    pytest.mark.skipif(cudnn.backend_version() < 91100, reason="cuDNN 9.10 and older still support compute capability below 7.5"),
+]
+
+_MESSAGE = "supports compute capability 7.5"
+
+
+def _conv_graph(sm_version):
+    graph = cudnn.pygraph(
+        io_data_type=cudnn.data_type.HALF,
+        intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        sm_version=sm_version,
+    )
+    x = graph.tensor(dim=[2, 8, 16, 16], stride=[2048, 1, 128, 8], data_type=cudnn.data_type.HALF)
+    w = graph.tensor(dim=[16, 8, 3, 3], stride=[72, 1, 24, 8], data_type=cudnn.data_type.HALF)
+    y = graph.conv_fprop(image=x, weight=w, padding=[1, 1], stride=[1, 1], dilation=[1, 1])
+    y.set_output(True)
+    graph.validate()
+    graph.build_operation_graph()
+    return graph
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sm_version", [52, 61, 70, 72])
+def test_cudnn_911_declines_a_pre_turing_target(sm_version):
+    graph = _conv_graph(sm_version)
+    with pytest.raises(cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError, match=_MESSAGE):
+        graph.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
+    with pytest.raises(cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError, match=_MESSAGE):
+        graph.check_support()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU to plan for")
+def test_cudnn_911_keeps_a_turing_target():
+    """SM75 is the oldest architecture cuDNN 9.11 supports: the gate leaves it alone."""
+    graph = _conv_graph(75)
+    try:
+        graph.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
+    except cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError as error:  # heuristics for a foreign target may decline on their own
+        assert _MESSAGE not in str(error)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (7, 5), reason="needs a GPU below compute capability 7.5")
+def test_cudnn_911_declines_the_current_pre_turing_device():
+    """Without sm_version the target is unset (-1); plan creation resolves it from the device before the gate, so a
+    graph that goes straight to build_plans() is declined there too, not only by check_support()."""
+    graph = _conv_graph(None)
+    with pytest.raises(cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError, match=_MESSAGE):
+        graph.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A, cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK])
